If arousal rises, let it rise. And if you like, take it back briefly, breathe out long, and let it grow again. There's no point at which anything has to happen.

Whenever you're ready, let the movement slow down. Rest your hand calmly again. Feel what's there: the pulsing, the warmth, the breath.

Finally, place a hand on your heart once more. Thank your body for this time. And when you're ready, slowly open your eyes.
lessons.reflection_question: What did you discover about yourself on this journey – and what would you like to feel again next time?

courses.title: 9. Female Desire and Body Knowledge
courses.subtitle: Pelvic floor, mental movies, anatomy and the cycle – knowledge that takes the pressure off.

lessons.title: The Female Pelvic Floor: Letting Go Instead of Holding On
lessons.summary: Why many women have a pelvic floor that tends to be too tense – and how targeted opening can help.
lessons.content:
Contracting can be easier to imagine than releasing. The pelvic floor needs both. After childbirth, with bladder weakness or with pain, training needs can differ considerably. This lesson brings attention to an area that may keep holding on when you would like to relax.

Why it works
A permanently tense pelvic floor can have consequences. First: pain on penetration or an involuntary contraction of the muscles at the vaginal entrance, known as vaginismus. Pleasant sensations and the ability to relax may also be affected. This alone does not explain why an orgasm might not occur.
On top of that comes the circle from course 1: if you expect pain, you tense up – and if you tense up, you feel more pain.

The exercise
Opening. Breathe deeply into your belly. As you breathe in, imagine the vaginal entrance and perineum becoming soft and gently yielding downwards and outwards, like a bud opening in the warmth. No pushing, just yielding. As you breathe out, everything stays soft.
Practise this for a few minutes every day, also with the pelvic floor timer. Over time, opening becomes something you can call on in intimate moments too.

When to see a doctor
Pain during sex, burning, or penetration not being possible at all can be treated well – but not with an app alone. A gynaecological examination and specialised pelvic floor physiotherapy can achieve a great deal.
lessons.reflection_question: In everyday life or when being touched, can you feel whether your pelvic floor softly yields or unconsciously closes up protectively?

lessons.title: Mental Movies and the Pressure to Be Quick Enough
lessons.summary: How the worry of taking too long or having to orgasm slows desire – and what really awakens it.
lessons.content:
Women can experience performance pressure too, even when it goes unspoken. While many men fear coming too soon or losing their erection, many women's mental movie circles around similar questions: “I'm taking too long, my partner is getting impatient.” “What do I look like in this position?” “I have to come now so he feels validated.”

Why it works
The sex educator Emily Nagoski has popularised two ideas that take a lot of pressure off here.
First: desire can arise in two ways. Spontaneous desire appears seemingly out of nowhere. Responsive desire only emerges in the encounter, through closeness and touch. Both occur in women and men and can vary with the situation. If you want to explore closeness, you can discover whether desire develops; its absence is not a reason to keep going.
Second: alongside appealing stimulation, inhibiting influences matter, as you explored in course 1. Stress, tiredness, to-do lists and shame put on the brakes. Safety, time and permission release them.

The exercise
Give yourself explicit permission, out loud or on paper: “I may take all the time my body needs. I don't have to come.”
And look at your most important brake: What would have to be different for you to feel more relaxed in that moment? A thought about it belongs in the reframing journal.
lessons.reflection_question: Which expectation or thought is your biggest inner brake when it comes to your own desire?

lessons.title: The Clitoris: Bigger Than You Think
lessons.summary: Why the clitoris is a whole system of erectile tissue – and why it takes time to awaken.
lessons.content:
The idea still persists that the clitoris is a small point at the top of the labia. In fact, the visible part is only the tip.

Why it works
The clitoris has visible and internal parts; its shape and size vary between bodies. Its legs and bulbs reach deep into the tissue beneath the labia and surround the vaginal entrance. Like the penis, it consists of tissue that fills with blood.
During arousal, blood flow and sensitivity change. How much time you want for comfortable touch is individual and can vary from day to day. You do not have to reach a particular anatomical state or be ready after a set number of minutes.

The exercise
Allow yourself, alone or together, to plan this time in explicitly. Don't begin at the tip, but around it: mons, labia, inner thighs. Course 18 shows exactly how, with an illustration.
Pay attention to the changes: warmth, fullness, wetness. They can tell you something about your physical response. You decide whether you want a particular touch.
lessons.reflection_question: How does it feel to think that plenty of time isn't a long wait, but simply anatomy?

lessons.title: The Cycle and Desire
lessons.summary: How hormones can change desire over the month – and why fluctuations are normal.
lessons.content:
You may notice days when you seek closeness and others when you would rather be alone. A menstrual cycle can play a part without setting a pattern you can recognise. This lesson invites you to get to know your experience rather than measure it against a calendar.

Why it works
Roughly, four phases can be described. But experience is very individual, and hormonal contraception, pregnancy, breastfeeding or menopause change the picture considerably.
During menstruation some women tend to withdraw, others experience a special sensitivity precisely then.
In the days afterwards oestrogen rises. Many feel more energy and curiosity.
Around ovulation many women experience their strongest desire; the body is often wetter then too.
After ovulation, progesterone typically rises in a natural cycle. This does not predict the kind of closeness you want or how strong your desire will be.
When couples know about these fluctuations, the feeling “something is wrong with me” often disappears. There are times for fire and times for embers.

The exercise
For two or three months, observe your desire and mood, for example with the app's daily check-in or a cycle app. Is there a pattern? Share it with your partner if you like.

When to see a doctor
Severe pain during your period, sudden persistent lack of desire or menopausal symptoms are a good reason for a conversation with a gynaecologist.
lessons.reflection_question: In which phase of your cycle do you most feel like passion, and when more like security and comfort?

lessons.title: Squirting: what we know and what we don’t
lessons.summary: Female ejaculation, squirting and urine leakage are not the same thing. What studies show, what is open, and why nobody has to experience it.
lessons.content:
An experience can bring curiosity and leave questions behind. With squirting, images and claims often crowd out the space for your own response. This lesson grew from a community question and separates what is known from what remains open.

Few topics come with as many claims as squirting. Here is what is established and what stays open.

Three terms that often get mixed up
Female ejaculation means a few millilitres of a thicker, milky secretion from the Skene glands next to the urethra. Squirting means a gush of clear, thin fluid, often ten millilitres or more. Coital incontinence is unwanted loss of urine during sex, a symptom of bladder and pelvic floor that can be treated. From the inside the lines cannot be drawn reliably. What matters is whether it bothers you.

What studies found
Small studies with five to seven women show: in squirting the fluid comes largely from the bladder but often also contains a share of gland secretion. The fluid studied consisted substantially of urine; gland secretion may also be present. Small participant numbers limit how far these results can be generalised.

What stays open
Whether a “G-spot” exists as a separate organ is disputed. What can be said safely: the front wall of the vagina lies close to the urethra, glands and parts of the clitoris, and these structures belong together. How common squirting is, nobody knows exactly; figures between 10 and 69 percent depend on whom you ask. It does not have to be linked to orgasm, and many orgasms come without fluid.

What is not true
Squirting is not a better orgasm and no proof of arousal, trust or love. The fountains in porn are staged. If you never experience it, you miss nothing. If you do, it takes no performance.

Feelings
At first many people feel shock, shame or the thought that they peed. That is common. How you feel about it may change. A calm, respectful response from your partner can make it easier to talk, without expecting a particular reaction from you.

When help makes sense
For burning when passing urine, blood in the urine, pain during sex, or unwanted loss of urine in daily life or during sex that bothers you, talk to a doctor. Pelvic floor training can help.
lessons.reflection_question: When exploring, what matters more to you: experiencing something specific, or feeling at ease, even if nothing happens?

lessons.title: The cervix: anatomy, sensations, caution
lessons.summary: What the cervix is, what research says about sensations and “cervical orgasms”, and why depth is no yardstick.
lessons.content:
Discussions of the cervix often come with sweeping promises. Here we begin with the body itself: location, sensitivity and differences in experience. This community question gets a framework in which curiosity and clear boundaries can sit alongside each other.

The cervix is the lower, narrow part of the womb and reaches into the top of the vagina. With a finger you can feel it as a firm bump with a small opening, the cervical os.

Anatomy, short and clear
The os is very narrow and usually filled with mucus. During sex nothing enters the womb; one presses against the cervix or the vaginal vault. The vagina is roughly seven to ten centimetres deep, with big differences. Position, tilt and mobility are individual. A womb tilted backwards is normal.

What happens during arousal
Well documented: the vagina lengthens and the womb rises a little. That creates more room. The often-quoted claim that the womb becomes much larger could not be confirmed in magnetic resonance studies. Deeper contact need not feel pleasant even during arousal. Your comfort determines whether and how far you wish to go.

Sensations
The cervix has a good nerve supply (pelvic nerve, hypogastric nerve and the vagus nerve, which bypasses the spinal cord). “Insensitive” is therefore wrong. That does not mean it is pleasurable for everyone. Many experience pressure there as neutral or unpleasant, and that is completely normal.

Is there a cervical orgasm?
There are credible reports of deep, slowly rising sensations. The research is thin: few small studies, mostly from one research group, for example with women after spinal cord injury, where the vagus nerve seems to play a role. It is not recognised as a separate type of orgasm, and there are no reliable figures on how often it occurs. You do not have to experience it, and it is not “deeper” or “better”. Some coaches and guides claim much more: that the cervix is numb in many people and “wakes up” through daily practice, or that special messenger substances are released. That is not proven.

Cycle and life phases
Around ovulation the cervix sits higher and is softer, before and during the period lower and firmer. Many feel depth as more painful on some days; this is individual. Dryness and discomfort can increase around menopause. A gynaecologist can help assess treatment options, which may include lubricant or local hormone treatment depending on the situation.

When help makes sense
Deep pain during sex can point to endometriosis, inflammation, cysts or tension. Bleeding after sex outside your period, discharge with an odour, fever or lower abdominal pain should be checked by a doctor. Do not “push through”.
lessons.reflection_question: How does pressure deep in the vagina feel to you, neutral, pleasant or rather unpleasant, and what follows from that for you?

courses.title: 10. Resetting Your Stimulation
courses.subtitle: How fast digital habits can change sensation – and how to retune your ability to feel.

lessons.title: Fast Stimuli and the Reward System
lessons.summary: Why the brain gets used to fast, changing stimuli – and why real closeness needs a different pace.
lessons.content:
A swipe, a new image, another video: digital stimulation can set a pace you hardly notice. This lesson invites you to slow down and take a look. What part does the screen play for you, and how do you feel afterwards?

Why it works
The brain's reward system reacts especially to what is new and unexpected. Clicking from video to video while alone delivers constant new stimuli. The research on this is not clear-cut, and pornography is not automatically a problem. But many men report that real closeness then feels less intense to them.
Two habits can play a role. First: the brain adjusts to fast image changes from a spectator's perspective instead of slow stimuli like scent, skin and closeness. Second: if time alone is mainly used to relieve stress quickly, the body learns: arousal means getting to the goal fast, with a firm grip. That fits the death-grip pattern from course 19.
These habits do not affect everyone's encounters in the same way. You can observe whether your experience changes when your habits change.

The exercise
For one week, observe without judgement: When do you reach for fast digital stimuli? Out of boredom, after stress, out of habit before going to sleep?
Then try, for a few weeks, spending time with yourself without a screen. The next lesson shows how that can work.

When to see a doctor
If you notice that you can no longer control your consumption and it weighs on you, counselling or therapy can help a lot.
lessons.reflection_question: What is your most common reason for reaching for fast digital stimuli in everyday life – and what would you actually need in that moment?

lessons.title: Time With Yourself, Rethought
lessons.summary: From quick stress relief to mindful feeling – four simple rules.
lessons.content:
Time with yourself can find a different rhythm. You leave the screen outside and stay with what your hands and body notice. Small differences that disappear in a hurry may become clearer. That is the purpose of this practice.

Why it works
What you practise alone, you take into encounters with a partner. If you enjoy yourself slowly, sensitively and with a soft pelvic floor when alone, you'll find it easier with someone else too. Noticing your arousal earlier can help you choose pauses more deliberately.

The exercise
Four rules for the coming weeks.
First: no screen. The phone stays outside. Just your body and your imagination.
Second: soft instead of firm. Pay attention to your buttocks and pelvic floor. As soon as you notice you're tensing to push arousal higher, breathe in deeply and consciously let go. And switch from a tight fist to an open hand with a suitable lubricant.
Third: the scale from one to ten. Use the numbers as personal reference points rather than levels you have to reach. At seven or eight, slow down and breathe calmly until you're back at about five. Then the next wave.
Fourth: no goal. Take ten to fifteen minutes. Orgasm may come, but it doesn't have to. The pelvic floor timer helps you practise letting go.

Consent and safety
This exercise is just for you. If you're in a relationship, it can be a relief to talk about what you're practising.
lessons.reflection_question: What changes in your sensations when you leave out the screen and deliberately halve the pace?

lessons.title: Audio Practice: Waves Instead of a Sprint
lessons.summary: A guided exercise for time alone: slowly, without a screen, with conscious letting go.
lessons.content:
You do this exercise alone, in a quiet place, with no phone within reach. Have a lubricant suitable for this use ready. I'll guide you. You can stop at any time.

Lie down comfortably. Close your eyes. Breathe deeply into your belly three times and out again slowly. As you breathe out, you may notice the weight of your pelvis resting on the surface beneath you.
Notice how your jaw feels. Let it relax. Let your tongue lie softly in your mouth. Release your buttocks. Release your pelvic floor, as if it were sinking downwards.

Now begin to touch yourself. Not where it has the strongest effect, but around it: belly, inner thighs, groin. Slowly. With an open hand, not a fist.
When you turn to your penis, take your time. Glide long and slow. Feel the warmth of your hand.

Imagine a scale from one to ten. One is completely calm, ten is the point of no return. Where are you right now? You don't need to change anything. Just notice.

Let your arousal rise, slowly, to about seven.
And now: hands still. Breathe out long. Consciously release your pelvic floor. Feel the wave ebb a little, to about five.
That's it.

Begin again. Slowly. Let the wave rise again. Notice whether you tense up to move forward faster. If so: breathe out, let go, carry on at a calm pace.
At seven: hold still again. Breathe out. Let go. Wait.

One more wave. Perhaps you notice that you can now hold seven for longer without it tipping over. You are practising noticing changes earlier and choosing when to pause. The numbers remain a guide, not a test.

From now on the time is yours. You may carry on, you may come, you may also simply stop and feel what's there. There is no goal.

When you're done, place a hand on your belly. Breathe calmly. Feel how your body feels now. Thank yourself for this time.
lessons.reflection_question: At which number on the scale do you notice that you start to tense up?

courses.title: 11. Prostate and Perineum: Anatomy and Approach
courses.subtitle: Why the area behind the scrotum can be a source of deep relaxation and pleasure – and how to approach it safely and without shame.

lessons.title: Anatomy Without Shame
lessons.summary: What the prostate is, why touching it feels different from the glans – and why that has nothing to do with sexual orientation.
lessons.content:
Hardly any area of the male body is as loaded with shame as the one behind the scrotum. Many men tense up at the mere thought of being touched there – because of cultural clichés or the worry about what it might say about them. The answer is simple: it says something about anatomy, not about orientation.

Why it works
The prostate is a gland about the size of a chestnut, located directly below the bladder and surrounding the urethra. It produces part of the seminal fluid. A so-called G-area is not a corresponding, clearly defined gland.
Through its nerves, the glans delivers fast, sharply defined stimuli. The prostate, by contrast, is embedded in a dense network of nerves in the pelvis. Some men describe touch there as deep and spreading through the pelvis. The nerve pathways alone cannot predict how it will feel.
There's also a somatic aspect: part of the pelvic floor lies around the prostate. Learning to soften there teaches a lot about the tension that often plays a role in erectile problems and early ejaculation – see course 7 and course 19.
Some men experience orgasms through the prostate that feel longer and less abrupt. That's a possibility, not a promise.

The exercise
For today, just a thought experiment. Notice which thoughts come up when you read the words prostate stimulation. If you like, write them in the app's reframing journal and ask yourself: Is this a fact – or an old image?

When to see a doctor
Pain in the pelvis or perineum, burning when urinating, or blood in the urine or semen should be seen by a doctor before you experiment with touch in this area.
lessons.reflection_question: Which thoughts or old images come up when you think of prostate stimulation – and could you replace them for a moment with curiosity about your own body?

lessons.title: The Perineum: The Bridge From the Outside
lessons.summary: How to reach the root of the erectile tissue and the prostate from the outside via the perineum – a careful, low-shame way in.
lessons.content:
You don't have to start inside to get to know the pleasure of your deep pelvis. Between scrotum and anus lies a bridge of skin a few centimetres long: the perineum.

Why it works
Directly beneath this skin lie the roots of the erectile tissue, pelvic floor muscles and nerve pathways that also lead to the prostate. Touch here combines arousal with grounding: many men experience it as deep and calming at the same time. With external touch too, you decide what feels comfortable and when you want to stop.

The exercise
First, warmth: during your next solo practice or together, put some warm oil or lubricant on your index and middle fingers. Instead of only stroking the shaft, move beneath the testicles onto the perineum.
Second, pressure: about halfway to the anus you'll feel a soft spot. Apply steady, gently pulsing pressure there with two fingertips, inwards and slightly forwards towards the pubic bone.
Third, breath: breathe deeply into your belly and consciously let your pelvic floor sink softly against your fingers. The pelvic floor timer in the app helps you tell contracting and letting go apart. You may notice warmth or a change in tension. It can also remain simply a touch.

Consent and safety
The pressure should be pleasant, never painful. With a partner, the person being touched decides how firm it may be. If pressure on the perineum causes pain, have it checked by a doctor.
lessons.reflection_question: While relaxing today, try placing two fingers calmly on your perineum and breathing deeply into your belly. Can you feel the tissue beneath moving along?

lessons.title: The Way Inside: Slowly, Safely, Without a Goal
lessons.summary: Preparation, hygiene, the exhale trick and the gentle come-hither movement – for a first inner approach to the prostate.
lessons.content:
If you're curious – alone or together – about exploring the prostate directly, three things decide whether it's a good experience: preparation, relaxation and slowness.

Why it works
The sphincter is designed to close when pressed from the outside. Pushing triggers counter-tension and pain – and with it, immediately, the brake from course 1. Calm breathing and time can support conscious release; they do not replace willingness or make penetration automatically possible. The principle of this whole program applies especially clearly here: pressure closes, safety opens.

The exercise
First, preparation: using the toilet and cleaning the outer skin can be part of preparation; a shower does not clean the rectum. Fingernails short and smooth, hands washed. A disposable glove gives many people a sense of safety. Use plenty of lubricant, because the rectum doesn't lubricate itself.
Second, the exhale: place the fingertip coated with a suitable lubricant on the outside of the anus without pressing. Breathe in deeply. As you breathe out, let the pelvic floor soften slightly downwards and outwards. Exactly in this moment the finger can slowly glide in a little – or you wait for the next breath.
Third, arriving and moving: the prostate may be felt through the front wall of the rectum towards the navel. Its position and accessibility vary; finding it is not a requirement for a worthwhile exploration. First let the finger rest calmly for a minute and breathe. Then stroke gently over it with the pad of your finger, as if beckoning someone towards you. At the same time the penis can be touched slowly on the outside with a flat hand. The breathing pacer helps you stay calm.
Many need several attempts until it feels good. There is no goal.

Consent and safety
Pain always means: stop. Never insert anything into the anus that doesn't have a flared base and isn't made for it – objects without a stop can slip into the bowel. If you use toys, choose an undamaged toy designed for anal use, with a secure stopper, and follow the manufacturer's guidance. After anal contact, wash hands or toys before they touch the vulva or mouth. With a partner: only at their explicit wish, and stoppable at any time.

When to see a doctor
With haemorrhoids, fissures, acute inflammation, after operations in the pelvic area or with persistent pain, ask a doctor first.
lessons.reflection_question: What would you need in terms of time, atmosphere or agreement to allow this experience entirely without pressure, for yourself or with your partner?

lessons.title: Spicy: Prostate Massage From the Inside
lessons.summary: Step by step to the prostate: with a finger or toy, safe, clean and pleasurable.
lessons.content:
Some parts of the body remain unfamiliar for years, even though they have always been our own. The prostate is one of them. It lies in front of the rectum, below the bladder, and may be felt through the front wall of the rectum; its position and accessibility vary. Some men find touch there especially intense, while others find little pleasure in it. Exploring begins with taking your time and noticing your own response.

Preparation
Relaxation is everything. A warm bath, going to the toilet beforehand, short fingernails, a disposable glove or finger cot, and lots of lube. Check the manufacturer's guidance on compatibility between lubricant and toy materials. Water-based lubricant is often a suitable choice.

The way in
Outside first: massage the perineum, circle the anus, press gently without entering. Only when the sphincter feels soft does a finger slide in slowly, on the out-breath. Pause briefly so the body can adjust.

Finding the prostate
The finger curls forwards, towards the navel. After a few centimetres you'll feel a firmer area about the size of a walnut. Stroke there gently, circle or press rhythmically, like a heartbeat. Don't thrust.

With a toy
For anal use, choose only toys designed for it, with an adequately flared base or secure retrieval feature. A curved shape alone does not make a toy safe. Insert slowly, then play with the pelvic floor: squeeze, release. Some toys move by themselves this way.

Combining
While the prostate is massaged, the other hand can stroke the penis. Many men experience this as especially intense.

Safety
Never go directly from the anus to the vagina or mouth without changing the glove or toy or washing thoroughly. Pain means stop immediately. Get blood or persistent discomfort checked by a doctor.

Extra spicy: how it sounds with dirty talk
“I'm deep inside you.” “Feel your cock twitch when I press here.” “Relax your ass, let me in.” “Come without me touching it.”

The task
Alone or together: take time for the outside part, at least ten minutes, before a finger slides in. The aim isn't climax but finding the prostate and feeling how it responds.
lessons.reflection_question: What helped you relax, and how did the prostate feel?

courses.title: 12. Breaking the Silence
courses.subtitle: How open words dissolve shame and shared calm noticeably lowers the pressure.

lessons.title: Why Hiding Doubles the Pressure
lessons.summary: Why trying not to let anything show is what really fuels the tension.
lessons.content:
Sometimes you only notice afterwards how quiet you became. Something went differently from what you hoped, and instead of saying so, you smiled, changed the subject or withdrew. Many people know moments like this. This lesson considers the effort of hiding and how a conversation might begin.

Why it works
That is deeply human and comes from an old shame: the fear of being seen as not good enough. But hiding costs energy. The mind has to manage two things at once: being aroused and relaxed – and at the same time keeping up a facade so the other person doesn't notice.
This double game presses hard on the brake from course 1. The more you try not to let anything show, the louder your heart pounds. On top of that: without words, the other person often relates the silence to themselves – “Is it me?” That creates pressure on both sides that nobody talks about.
The way out isn't to explain everything, but to be calmly open.

The exercise
Remember a moment when you covered something up. What did you fear would happen if you said it out loud? Write the thought in the reframing journal and check it: How likely is that really? And what would be the worst, the best and the most likely outcome?
The next lesson gives you concrete sentences for exactly these moments.
lessons.reflection_question: How do you typically react after a difficult moment – do you withdraw, or do you talk about it?

lessons.title: Opening the Conversation
lessons.summary: Concrete sentences to raise the topic lightly and in a connecting way – before, during and after.
lessons.content:
Many people don't raise the topic because they fear a long, heavy problem talk. But openness doesn't have to be a drama. It's not about justifying yourself, but about an invitation to relax.

Why it works
A simple sentence can interrupt the double task from the previous lesson. Your partner has a chance to ask instead of having to interpret your silence. Closeness can grow from this, even if the conversation feels unfamiliar at first.

The exercise
Three sentence templates for three moments. Adapt them to your own way of speaking.
Before, for example while cuddling: “My head is pretty full today. It has nothing to do with you. Let's just kiss and cuddle, with no goal. If more happens, lovely – if not, the closeness is my highlight.”
In the middle, when arousal fades or your heart is racing: “My body needs a little break from overthinking right now. Let's just lie close and breathe.” Said with a smile, it means: everything is fine.
The next day, over coffee: “Thank you for being so relaxed yesterday. It feels good to know I don't have to put on a show with you.”
Choose one sentence and try it at the next opportunity.

Consent and safety
Openness works both ways. If {P:your partner} confides something like this in you: listen, don't fix, don't play it down. A simple “Thank you for telling me” is enough.
lessons.reflection_question: Which of the three sentences feels most natural for you to try at the next opportunity?

lessons.title: Finding Calm Together
lessons.summary: How two nervous systems can calm each other – and a simple exercise for it.
lessons.content:
Fighting your own restlessness alone in bed leaves you on your own. But humans are built to calm each other. Specialists call this co-regulation.

Why it works
The quiet presence of someone you trust can make it easier to settle. Comfortable contact and an audible breath give your attention somewhere to rest together. Your breathing patterns can remain different. Closeness need not be synchronised to feel connected.

The exercise
The shared heart breath. Lie close together. Each of you places a hand on the other's heart. You don't need to talk.
For two minutes, breathe together deeply into the belly and out again very slowly. The app's breathing pacer can set the rhythm.
Notice how your jaw, shoulders and pelvis change over time.
Feel free to suggest the exercise with no sexual intention at all, as a small ritual before falling asleep. That can give it a familiar place in your everyday life.
lessons.reflection_question: Can you imagine suggesting the shared heart breath simply as a cuddling ritual – with no ulterior motive at all?

courses.title: 13. Mismatched Desire: When One Wants It More Often
courses.subtitle: Why desire is rarely evenly distributed – and how to get out of pushing and avoiding.

lessons.title: Not a Defect: Why Desire Is Rarely Evenly Distributed
lessons.summary: Different levels of desire are the normal case in relationships, not the problem.
lessons.content:
You seek intimacy when your partner doesn't. Or you sense a wish coming towards you that you have no room for yet. Different levels of desire can quickly feel like a verdict on the relationship. To begin with, they describe two people having different experiences.

Why this happens
Desire isn't a fixed quantity like shoe size. It fluctuates with stress, sleep, health, life phase and the mood in the relationship. Two people who by chance always want the same amount would be the exception.
On top of that, desire can arise in two ways. With spontaneous desire, the wanting comes first, often seemingly out of nowhere. With responsive desire, it only arises once closeness, touch or arousal are already there. Many people, especially in long relationships, mainly experience the responsive form. Those who feel this way rarely think of sex on their own – but can enjoy it a lot when the way in is right.
And finally the dual control model from course 1: desire arises when there is enough accelerator and little on the brake. Lower desire can reflect both a lack of appealing stimulation and inhibiting influences. The latter may include tiredness, pressure, unresolved anger, the feeling of having to perform.

The exercise
Each of you take ten minutes on your own and answer three questions in writing:
When in recent months did I feel desire most – and what was different then?
Do I know spontaneous desire, responsive desire, or both?
What is pressing my brake most right now?
Then share, without discussing. The other only listens and at most asks follow-up questions. The aim isn't to solve a problem, but to understand how desire works for the other.

Consent and safety
Nobody has to justify their desire, whether it's high or low. If your desire has dropped markedly and permanently and that distresses you, it's worth talking to a doctor: hormones, medications such as some antidepressants, the thyroid, depression or pain can be behind it.
lessons.reflection_question: Is your desire more spontaneous or more responsive – and what is pressing your brake right now?

lessons.title: The Vicious Circle of Pushing and Avoiding
lessons.summary: How two loving people take away each other's desire without meaning to.
lessons.content:
Different levels of desire can become caught in a cycle: the one who wants more asks, hints, tries. The one who wants less feels pressured and avoids – goes to bed earlier, avoids kisses that might lead somewhere. The other then feels rejected and pushes more. And so on.

Why this happens
Both are acting for good reasons. The one who wants more is often looking not only for sex, but for reassurance: I'm desirable, we're close. A no may then feel like personal rejection, even when it is not intended that way.
The one who wants less experiences every approach as an expectation. And expectation is a powerful brake pedal. That's why at some point even harmless tenderness disappears, because every touch could seem like an invitation.
The result: one feels unloved, the other under pressure. And both have less closeness than before.

The exercise
First: give the circle a name, for example “our merry-go-round”. When you notice it starting, either of you may say: “We're on the merry-go-round again.” That takes the blame out of the moment.
Second: separate tenderness and sex for two weeks. Kisses, hugs and cuddling are explicitly allowed and explicitly lead nowhere. Agree on which kinds of affection are welcome right now. The arrangement should offer both of you clarity without creating a new expectation of touch.
Third: practise the friendly no. Instead of “No, I'm tired”, for example: “Not for sex tonight, but I'd love to fall asleep in your arms.” A no to sex isn't a no to the person.

Consent and safety
Nobody owes the other sex, and nobody has to beg for closeness. If a no leads to accusations, silence or pressure, that's a topic for a calm conversation or couples counselling.
lessons.reflection_question: How do you notice that you're on the merry-go-round – and what could you do differently next time?

lessons.title: The Pleasure Menu: More Than Yes or No
lessons.summary: Having more options between sex and nothing means saying yes more often.
lessons.content:
An invitation to intimacy can mean many things. Sometimes what might follow stays unspoken, and a kiss seems to carry the weight of a whole evening. A shared pleasure menu gives smaller possibilities names of their own. You can say more clearly what appeals to you right now.

Why it works
The partner with less desire often isn't rejecting closeness, but the prospect of something big, long and strenuous. With small, clearly limited invitations, the brake is much quieter. And because responsive desire only arises along the way, a small invitation sometimes turns into more – without it having to.

The exercise
Together, write a menu with three sections.
Starters, five to ten minutes: for example long kisses, showering together, lying naked and cuddled up, a neck massage.
Main courses: touch without a goal like the shared evening in this app, a hand job for one of you, oral sex, sex.
Desserts for low-energy days: one touches themselves while the other holds them, or simply falling asleep together.
Each of you marks what you currently like, what maybe, what not. Hang the menu somewhere only you two see it, or save it on your phone.
From now on the invitation is no longer “Do you feel like it?”, but “Would you like something from the menu?”. And the partner with less desire may choose too: “A starter works tonight.”

Consent and safety
A starter is a starter. Choosing it doesn't promise a main course. That's exactly what makes the menu safe. If you'd like ideas: the yes/no/maybe list in the couple channel helps fill it.
lessons.reflection_question: What's on your personal starter menu – small things you could almost always say yes to?

lessons.title: Conditions for Desire: What Releases Your Brake
lessons.summary: Desire itself can't be planned – but the circumstances under which it can arise can.
lessons.content:
Desire can't be ordered. But you can create the conditions under which it arises more easily. This is something to explore together, with room for both perspectives.

Why it works
When the brake is the problem, more accelerator doesn't help much. An even more seductive offer changes nothing when the head is full of appointments or an argument from yesterday is still echoing. Knowing your brakes and making them smaller together gives desire room.
Time set aside for closeness also has a bad reputation it doesn't deserve. An evening set aside can give you time to settle together without deciding what has to happen. Many couples experience scheduled evenings as more relaxed.

The exercise
Each of you writes two lists. My brakes: what takes my desire away, for example an untidy bedroom, tiredness, the feeling that sex is expected, unresolved anger. My accelerator: what awakens desire, for example time without phones, a conversation, having laughed together, being freshly showered, compliments that don't want anything.
Read your lists to each other. Then choose one brake per person that you can make smaller together, and one accelerator you'll build in this week.
If you like, agree on one evening a week as your time: with no obligation to have sex, but with time for closeness. The shared evening in the app can be a start.

Consent and safety
The lists are gifts, not demands. If you notice you can't get further on your own, couples or sex counselling isn't a sign of failure, but a way to find a path forward together.
lessons.reflection_question: Which one brake could you make smaller together this week?

courses.title: 14. Life Phases: Desire in Transition
courses.subtitle: After birth, in menopause, over the years and in illness – what changes and what helps.

lessons.title: After Birth: A New Body, a New Couple
lessons.summary: Why desire often takes a break after giving birth – and how closeness can stay anyway.
lessons.content:
After giving birth, much is different: the body, sleep, everyday life, your role as a couple. That sex moves into the background for a while is not a warning sign, but entirely ordinary.

Why this happens
The body is healing. Birth injuries, a caesarean or an overstretched pelvic floor need time. While breastfeeding, oestrogen levels are low. As a result the mucous membranes are often drier and more sensitive, and desire can be quieter. On top of that come lack of sleep and the feeling of having been touched all day already.
The partner also experiences the new time differently: some long for closeness as reassurance, others are exhausted or unsure themselves.

The exercise
First: talk about closeness, not just about sex. What are you both missing right now? Often it's time for two, a conversation that isn't about the baby, a hug without ulterior motives.
Second: when you want to sleep together again, start slowly. Plenty of water-based lubricant, positions in which the woman sets depth and pace, and permission to stop at any time.
Third: ask your midwife or pelvic floor physiotherapist how to begin training in a way that fits your recovery. Awareness, contraction and release all matter; an app timer cannot replace an individual postnatal assessment.

Consent and safety
When sex is possible again is decided by the woman's body, not the calendar. Have a check-up with your gynaecologist or midwife beforehand. Pain that persists, incontinence or a lasting low mood belong in medical hands; pelvic floor physiotherapy and help with postnatal depression are readily available.
lessons.reflection_question: What form of closeness would feel good to both of you right now, without sex at all?

lessons.title: Menopause: When Desire Changes
lessons.summary: What falling oestrogen does to desire and the body – and what really helps.
lessons.content:
The menopausal transition can unfold over years. Your sleep may change, touch may feel different, or desire may find another rhythm. Your sexuality can change with you. Pregnancy is still possible during perimenopause; seek individual advice on when contraception is no longer needed.

Why this happens
With falling oestrogen, the vaginal lining becomes thinner and drier. Sex can then burn or hurt even though the desire is there. Hot flushes and poor sleep drain energy. Some women feel less desire, others experience their desire more freely than before.
Important: dryness is not a sign of lacking arousal. Mind and mucous membranes are often no longer in step during this time.

The exercise
First: use lubricant generously, ideally from the start and not only once it chafes. For daily care there are vaginal moisturisers.
Second: more time to get started. Arousal now often takes longer, and that's fine. The courses on slowness and the shared evening suit this phase well.
Third: talk about it as a couple. What has changed becomes easier when both know and nobody takes the change personally.

Consent and safety
You don't have to endure pain during sex. A gynaecologist can check whether local oestrogen treatment is an option; it works directly on the mucous membranes. Good treatment options also exist for severe hot flushes, sleep problems or low moods.
lessons.reflection_question: What has changed in your body that your partner doesn't know about yet?

lessons.title: Over the Years: Slower, but Not Less
lessons.summary: How arousal changes with age – and why slowing down is an opportunity.
lessons.content:
Over the years, desire can change: its pace, its beginnings, the time you need to recover. You may miss familiar responses and discover new freedoms. Both can be true. What matters is finding a sexuality that fits your body and life as they are today.

Why this happens
In men, the erection often needs more direct touch and more time. It's sometimes less firm, and after orgasm it takes longer until the next one. In women, arousal often takes longer and the mucous membranes become more sensitive.
On top of that come blood pressure, diabetes, weight, smoking and medication. Vascular health matters to both the heart and the pelvis. That's why with erectile problems a look at heart health is always worthwhile.
What often gets better with the years: experience, composure, less performance pressure and the ability to enjoy the moment.

The exercise
First: away from the goal. When penetration is no longer the automatic centre, the rest becomes more important: hands, mouth, skin, time. Many couples rediscover exactly through this what they like.
Second: an appointment for pleasure. When energy is scarcer, a time of day when you're both awake helps – often that's in the morning or during the day at weekends, not late at night.
Third: breathe calmly. The breathing pacer in the app calms the nervous system; a relaxed body responds more easily.

Consent and safety
Have erectile problems, pain or marked changes checked by a doctor before trying remedies. Erectile dysfunction medication and other drugs only after medical advice, especially if you take heart medication.
lessons.reflection_question: What has become better in your sex life over the years – and have you ever told each other?

lessons.title: Illness, Medication and Crises
lessons.summary: When body or mind have other worries right now – and closeness should still keep its place.
lessons.content:
A serious illness, depression, a loss, a crisis at work: in times like these desire often has no room. That is understandable and not a personal failure. If it troubles you, you can still seek support.

Why this happens
The body sets priorities. Under constant stress, the brake from course 1 is pressed all the way down. Illnesses such as diabetes, heart and vascular disease, cancer or chronic pain act directly on arousal and sensation.
Medication also plays a big role. Some antidepressants, certain blood pressure drugs, hormonal contraception and many others can change desire, arousal or orgasm. Anyone who doesn't know this looks for the fault in themselves or in the relationship.

The exercise
First: renegotiate closeness. What works right now, what doesn't? Perhaps just holding, stroking, lying side by side. Talk about it so nobody has to guess.
Second: sort your thoughts. If sentences like “I'm not a real woman anymore” or “I'm just a burden” follow you, write them in the app's thought journal and check them as in course 4.
Third: ask the question at your next medical appointment: Can what I'm taking affect my desire? Doctors are familiar with this question.

Consent and safety
Never stop medication on your own, even if you suspect side effects. Often there are alternatives or different doses. If you feel low, hopeless or without drive for weeks, get medical or psychotherapeutic help. In an acute crisis, contact a crisis line or emergency services in your country; in Germany the Telefonseelsorge is available around the clock on 0800 111 0 111.
lessons.reflection_question: What form of closeness is possible for you even in difficult times?

courses.title: 15. Anticipation and Slowness
courses.subtitle: Why expectation without pressure is one of the strongest erotic tools – and how to turn differing desire into tension instead of frustration.

lessons.title: The Ninety-Percent Principle: Anticipation Instead of Obligation
lessons.summary: How small, deliberately unfinished moments in everyday life awaken desire – without the expectation that they must lead to sex.
lessons.content:
In many long relationships, everyday life knows only two switch positions: the fleeting kiss on the way out the door – or the evening in bed when “the full programme” is silently expected. There's little in between. This in-between space can have an appeal of its own: closeness that can linger briefly without deciding the rest of the evening.

Why it works
Remember the dual control model from course 1: desire needs an accelerator that is engaged and a brake that isn't pressed. The all-or-nothing pattern presses the brake. As soon as a touch is read as the start of sex, many immediately hear the question “Do I have to now?” or “Will it work this time?” – the spectator trap from course 4.
A moment that both know will end shortly takes this pressure out. Nobody has to deliver, nobody has to refuse. At the same time it engages the accelerator: the brain's reward system reacts particularly strongly to anticipation – to something that is in prospect but not yet fulfilled. And anyone with more responsive desire, meaning desire that only arises through closeness rather than being there spontaneously, gets small sparks spread through the day instead of a single cold start in the evening.

The exercise
Together, agree on a playful rule: in everyday life you may meet each other briefly and deliberately sensually – and stop before it really gets going. “Ninety percent” is a playful image, not a measurable level of arousal: end the moment at a point that feels comfortable to both of you.
An example: in the kitchen in the morning you take your partner in your arms for a slow, intimate kiss, let your hands wander calmly over back and hips and the two of you take a few breaths together. After about a minute you let go, smile and leave. No comment about later, no “to be continued”.
The ending without a promise is what matters. If the moment turns into more in the evening, lovely. If not, the exercise still worked: you experienced closeness without it having to lead anywhere.

Consent and safety
Discuss the rule beforehand instead of surprising each other with it. What feels playful to one can feel intrusive to the other – for example when someone is stressed, tired or just not in the mood. Agree on a simple sign with which either of you can say “not today” at any time without having to explain, and accept it without disappointment. Pressure-free works both ways: the game itself must never become an obligation.
lessons.reflection_question: How does your body react when you know a touch will end again shortly – and what changes when it's supposed to lead somewhere?

lessons.title: The Art of Slow Motion
lessons.summary: Why radically slowing down sharpens perception, takes the pressure out and makes touch more intense.
lessons.content:
Feeling insecure in bed often makes people fast. Speed, firm rubbing and hectic movements drown out subtle feeling – a bit like loud music meant to cover up nervousness. Small differences in touch may get lost in the rush. Another pace gives you a chance to notice them again.

Why it works
A slower movement can bring details into focus: where contact begins, how warm the skin is, when pressure changes. Some find this calming; others soon want more pace. Either response can tell you what suits the moment.
For men this often means: the worry of coming too soon gets quieter because the stimulus stays controllable. And if the erection softens a little in between, that's no problem at this pace. For women it often means: the body has time to open and go along instead of bracing against speed.

The exercise
At your next encounter, try slowing your usual pace to about a tenth. Whether with the hand, with the mouth or while making love: so slowly that from the outside you can barely see anything moving.
Consciously feel: Where exactly is there contact right now? How warm is it? What changes with every millimetre?
Make it a game: whoever gets impatient and wants to speed up is gently held by the hips by the other and brought back into slow motion. The pelvic floor timer in the app can help keep the pelvis soft.

Consent and safety
Slowness is an offer, not a rule that has to be kept up to the end. If one of you needs something else, say so. And impatience isn't a mistake. It can be a reason to ask for another pace or a pause.
lessons.reflection_question: How does it feel to imagine, next time, not thrusting but merging only through tiny movements and breathing together?

lessons.title: Anticipation in Everyday Life: The Art of Hinting
lessons.summary: Desire doesn't begin in the bedroom, but hours earlier – with small signs.
lessons.content:
For many couples, sex only begins when they're lying in bed. Then everyday life is supposed to turn into desire within a few minutes. For many people, especially those with responsive desire, that's too short a run-up.

Why it works
Anticipation is already desire. Anticipation can be pleasurable before anything happens. Small hints spread over the day keep the accelerator from course 1 gently pressed without building pressure. Arriving in the evening, you're then not starting from zero.

The exercise
Choose three small hints for one day, for example:
in the morning a longer kiss than usual that deliberately doesn't go further;
at midday a spark in this app's couple channel, such as “Looking forward to later”;
in the afternoon a sentence that only means something to the two of you, or a look across the table.
The ninety-percent rule from the first lesson matters: every hint stays a hint. Something may happen in the evening – but it doesn't have to. That's exactly what keeps the anticipation relaxed.

Consent and safety
Hints are invitations, not announcements. If the other person would rather just cuddle in the evening, the day was still lovely. And the spark “Rather not today” in the couple channel is just as welcome as any other.
lessons.reflection_question: Which small hint would warm you most in everyday life?

courses.title: 16. Everyday Eroticism: Desire Between Coffee and Calendar
courses.subtitle: How to keep desire alive in everyday life: small gestures, anticipation, rituals, games, beautiful lingerie and striptease. In spicy mode with hot messages, quickies and a day full of tension.

lessons.title: The Erotic Climate
lessons.summary: Why desire rarely appears in the evening but grows over the day, and which small gestures warm the climate.
lessons.content:
Many couples wait for the perfect evening: time, calm, mood. And wonder why it comes so rarely. The small moments in between can matter too: an attentive glance, a touch, time to listen. They can nurture a sense of being desired and of staying connected through an ordinary day. You could call it the erotic climate.

What warms the climate
Touches in passing: a hand on the neck, the back, the hip, without it having to lead to more.
The long kiss: instead of a quick peck when you greet each other, a kiss that lasts a few seconds. Long enough to really arrive.
Looks: looking at the other when they don't expect it, and showing it.
Compliments: concrete and honest, including about the body. “Those trousers suit you.” “I love how you smell.”
Attention: putting the phone away when the other is talking.

What cools the climate
Constant organising without a break, criticism in front of others, touch only when sex is wanted. If you only get tender when you want something, touch becomes a question that sometimes has to be answered with no. Touch without intention takes away that pressure.

The task
Choose three small gestures to do every day for a week: for example the long kiss when you greet each other, a touch in passing and a compliment. Without expecting it to lead to sex. At the end of the week, talk about what has changed.

For singles
There's an erotic climate on your own too: how you treat your body, what you wear, how you move. The fifth lesson looks at this.
lessons.reflection_question: Which small gesture made the biggest difference this week, for you or for your partner?

lessons.title: Anticipation Through the Day
lessons.summary: How one sentence in the morning can make the whole day crackle, and why anticipation is often half the pleasure.
lessons.content:
Anticipation is an underrated part of desire. If you know something lovely is waiting in the evening, you keep thinking about it during the day, and your body starts to prepare. Many people, especially those with more responsive desire, get in the mood exactly like this: not out of nowhere, but because something was set in motion.

The art of the hint
A hint doesn't give everything away, it makes you curious. A sentence at breakfast: “I've got plans for you tonight.” A look that lasts a little too long. A hand that slips a little lower than usual when you say goodbye. Your partner doesn't know exactly what's coming, only that something is.

Anticipation without pressure
Important: a hint is an invitation, not a promise that has to be kept. If tiredness wins in the evening after all, that's fine. Then you cuddle, or the anticipation moves on to the next day. If anticipation feels like an obligation, it's quickly lost.

The task
On one day this week, each of you sends the other a hint in the morning, as a sentence, a note or a message. No details, just an invitation to closeness. In the evening you decide together what becomes of it.
Ideas for the note: “I'm looking forward to your skin tonight.” “Keep the evening free.” “I thought about you earlier, and not in a family-friendly way.”

If you have little time
Anticipation doesn't need a whole evening. Even twenty minutes after the children are in bed can feel like a date if you've been looking forward to it all day.
lessons.reflection_question: How did it feel to go through the day with a hint on your mind?

lessons.title: Rituals Against Routine
lessons.summary: Fixed times for closeness, a bed without phones and dates at home: why planning isn't unromantic.
lessons.content:
“Sex has to be spontaneous” is one of the most stubborn myths. At the start of a relationship much was spontaneous, because being in love pushed everything else aside. In everyday life with work, children and tiredness, everyday life pushes desire aside. Rituals create the space in which spontaneity becomes possible again.

A fixed time, not a fixed routine
Agree on a fixed evening each week that belongs only to you. Important: what you agree on is the time, not sex. You can talk, massage, bathe, kiss, or sleep together. Without pressure for anything in particular to happen. Many couples find that this is exactly what brings desire back.

The bed as your place
Screens can take up much of the time you spend beside each other. You may want to explore how that space feels without distraction. Try it for a week: phones stay outside the bedroom, an alarm clock replaces the phone.

Dates at home
A date doesn't have to be expensive. Cook together, set the table, put on something nice, put on music. Treat each other as if you had just started dating. Ask each other things you don't yet know about one another.

The task
Choose one ritual and try it for two weeks: the fixed evening, the phone-free bed or a date at home each week. Put the ritual in your calendar, so your time together has a visible place in everyday life.

If a ritual doesn't fit
Then change it. Rituals should serve you, not the other way round. Some couples prefer a fixed morning, others a midday at the weekend.
lessons.reflection_question: Which ritual really fits your everyday life, and what would you have to leave out for it?

lessons.title: Little Games for In Between
lessons.summary: Code words, secrets and touches under the table: games that make everyday life tingle.
lessons.content:
A word only the two of you understand can briefly change an ordinary day. A glance, a smile you try to hide: playful eroticism can live in this small shared understanding. The following ideas give it a place in daily life.

The code word
Agree on a harmless word that means something completely different to the two of you: for example “pineapple” for “I want you tonight”. If it comes up at dinner with friends or on the phone, only you two know what it means.

The secret
One of you wears something only the other knows about: special underwear, no underwear at all, a perfume that otherwise only appears in the bedroom. All day long your partner knows about it, and perhaps looks at you a little differently.

Touches nobody sees
A hand on the thigh under the table, a finger stroking the palm while you walk, a whisper in the ear while shopping. Always so that nobody else notices and nobody feels bothered, and only if it feels right for both of you.

The compliment game
Every day a compliment about the body, on a note left where the other will find it: in their wallet, on the mirror, in a jacket pocket.

The task
Choose two games and play them for a week. Feel free to invent your own. Notice how it feels to share a secret.

Limits
Games live from both wanting to play. What feels tingly to one person may feel embarrassing to the other, especially in front of acquaintances or colleagues. Briefly agree beforehand where the limits are.
lessons.reflection_question: Which game made you laugh or crackle the most?

lessons.title: Staying Erotic on Your Own
lessons.summary: Sensuality in your own everyday life: how to stay in touch with yourself, in a relationship or on your own.
lessons.content:
Eroticism isn't only something that happens between two people. It starts with your relationship to yourself: how you perceive your body, how you treat it, how often you allow yourself pleasure. If you're in sensual contact with yourself, you bring that aliveness into a relationship, and if you live alone, you don't have to go without it.

Sensuality in everyday life
The shower: not rushed, but a few minutes with warm water on your skin and a shower gel that smells good.
Clothes: wearing something you feel good in, even on perfectly ordinary days.
Music: a song that moves you, and moving to it, alone in the kitchen.
Food: eating slowly, tasting, smelling. Enjoyment is a skill you can practise.
Touch: putting on lotion as if you were someone you like.

Masturbation as self-care
Touching yourself isn't a substitute for sex with another person, but its own form of closeness to yourself. If you know what you like, you can show it. And if you regularly allow yourself pleasure, you often feel more alive in everyday life too.

The task
This week, plan an hour just for you and your body: a bath, music, candles, lotion, and if you like, the guided body journey below this lesson. Treat it like a date you're looking forward to.

In a relationship
Time with yourself is valuable in a partnership too. You can talk together about making room for both personal time and time as a couple. Many couples find that their own desire enlivens their shared desire as well.
lessons.reflection_question: When did you last deliberately allow yourself pleasure just for you, and how did it feel?

lessons.title: Nicely wrapped: lingerie in everyday life
lessons.summary: Beautiful lingerie doesn't belong in the drawer: as a secret under your clothes, as a gift and for slow unwrapping.
lessons.content:
Sexy lingerie is often saved for special occasions: the anniversary, the holiday, Valentine's Day. And then it spends most of its time in the drawer. Yet it can do a lot in everyday life, as a little secret, as a gift and as an invitation.

The secret under your clothes
Beautiful lingerie beneath ordinary clothes can give the day a small secret. In the meeting, at the supermarket, at the bus stop: only you know what you're wearing underneath. Give your partner a small hint in the morning and it turns into anticipation. "I'm wearing something today you haven't seen yet." That's all it takes.

The unwrapping
Lingerie is wrapping, and unwrapping is one of the loveliest games there is. Take your time: a strap that slowly slides off a shoulder, a shirt opened button by button, a hand that first strokes over the fabric and then beneath it. Whoever is being unwrapped may simply enjoy it, without helping.

Lingerie as a gift
Giving lingerie is a lovely gesture, but also a delicate one. It can quickly feel as if you're supposed to look different from how you look now. A few rules help:
Know the size, don't guess. Check together, or choose together.
Gift the other person's taste, not just your own.
The gift is an invitation, not an obligation. It may stay in the drawer.
Men enjoy lingerie as a gift too, often precisely because they don't expect it.

Men wrap themselves up too
Nice, well-fitting underwear instead of the worn-out pair, a shirt she'd love to unbutton, a well-kept beard, a scent: dressing up for the other person shows that you want to be desired. For many, that is one of the most attractive messages of all.

Comfort comes first
Underwear that pinches, itches or constantly needs adjusting kills any desire. Better a comfortable, beautiful piece than a spectacular one you can't move in.

The exercise
On one day this week, each of you wears something special under your clothes and gives a small hint in the morning. In the evening, there's unwrapping, slowly, and without expecting it to lead to more.

For singles
The secret is worth it on your own, too. Wear something beautiful just for yourself and notice what it does to your day.
lessons.reflection_question: How did the day with a secret under your clothes feel, and how did the unwrapping in the evening feel?

lessons.title: A striptease to try
lessons.summary: Slowly undressing for your partner, without dance lessons and without perfection: a striptease for women and men.
lessons.content:
A striptease sounds like a stage, a pole and someone who has practised for years. At home it's about something else entirely: that you show yourself, at your own pace, and that your partner watches you. That's exciting, for both sides. And it doesn't take a single dance lesson.

Why a striptease works
Whoever undresses decides what their partner sees and when. Taking on that role can be very empowering, especially for people who struggle with their body. And whoever watches experiences something that almost never happens in everyday life: time to simply look at the other person.

The preparation
The music: two or three songs you like with a calm, steady beat. Slower is almost always better.
The light: dimmed, warm, a few candles. Bright enough to see something, dark enough for you to feel comfortable.
The clothes: several layers that open easily. A shirt or blouse with buttons, a skirt or trousers with a zip, beautiful lingerie underneath. If you like, take your socks off first so you can move more easily.
The chair: your partner sits comfortably and watches.

How it can go
Arriving: stand in front of your partner, look at them, breathe. Move to the music, just a little, with your hips and shoulders.
Opening slowly: one button after another. Pause in between and seek their gaze. The waiting is the real thrill.
Turning: turn your back to your partner, let a piece of clothing slide off your shoulder, look back over your shoulder.
Coming closer: walk up to your partner, take their hand and briefly place it on your skin, then step back again.
The end: how far you go is your decision. Down to the lingerie, all the way naked, or you let them undress you the rest of the way.

For men
Men can undress too, and many partners find it very appealing, precisely because it rarely happens. A shirt opened button by button, a belt slowly pulled out of the trousers, a look while doing it: that's quite enough. Self-irony is allowed and often makes it even more attractive.

If you have to laugh
Then laugh. A button that sticks, a leg that gets caught in the trousers: it's all part of it. A striptease with laughter hasn't failed, it's real. Just pick up where you left off.

For the person watching
Look, fully. Show that you like it, with a smile, a sigh, a word. Don't touch unless you're invited. And afterwards: an honest compliment about what you liked best.

The exercise
Choose an evening when one person does a striptease for the other. Next time you swap. If you don't dare yet, start with a single piece of clothing, for example a shirt that is slowly opened.

For singles
Try it in front of the mirror, just for you. You may see your body differently for a moment: in motion, at your own pace, through a gaze that belongs to you.
lessons.reflection_question: What was it like to show yourself or to watch, and which moment had the most sizzle?

lessons.title: Hot Messages
lessons.summary: Sexting with style and safety: how hot messages charge up the day, and what to keep in mind.
lessons.content:
